data.long_meaning: Mahima is a Sanskrit word that signifies greatness, majesty, or glory. It is revered in Hinduism as a divine quality, representing the power and might of the universe. The name Mahima carries the meaning “Greatness, Majesty” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mahima usually hope their child will grow to embody greatness, majesty and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Mahima, also known as Mahima Devi, was a 16th-century Hindu saint and philosopher, born in the Indian state of Bihar. She is considered a reincarnation of the goddess Saraswati and is revered for Her wisdom and devotion to the god Vishnu. Mahima is known to have lived during the late Mughal period, around the end of the 16th century.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Mahima is found in the Puranic texts of Hinduism, specifically in the Mahabharata. In this text, Mahima is mentioned as the name of a divine entity, a goddess who embodies the qualities of compassion, grace, and power. Her significance is linked to the story of the god Krishna, and She is believed to have appeared during the Mahabharata war period, around the 3rd or 4th century BCE.
